title: Stuttgart radio band in Germany
summary: The family moved to Stuttgart to lead a radio band, then fought a pension and dismissal dispute.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So Sperry, in the Army, --we had a singer named Anita Derian who was the girlfriend of a German who had come here as a kid, he became an American citizen, served in the Army and all that, whose mother was an actress in Germany before the war. They had run ahead of the Nazis all the way through--the Jewish people--and wound up in Turkey where they managed to survive somehow through the war, and at the end of it was one of those exchange kids. They rought them here because they weren't eating over there.

So around '55 or so, I think the mother got him a position in Sutgart in radio as a producer and went back there and there met Sperry. Now meanwhile, we have this girl singer and Sperry in our band and they struck up a thing and as it turns out, those radio stations each had a house group--

Yes. And the one in (inaudible) was moving, so there was an opening and Peter Mordo said, why not me, why not Eddie, because they're not doing anything now--or Sperry said why not Eddie, because Sperry had met a very beautiful German girl and really wanted to stay in Germany and didn't know how to bring it about, so he figured this was a way to do it. That must have been in the back of his mind.
Again, it was one of those things I couldn't refuse; they wanted to do it, so we put the whole family on a boat and over we went.

But there were things involved, they have a law in Germany where they become eligible for pension if a band is signed to the station. They were using me as an independent contractor and the band didn't want this. I didn't know that, so they began doing everything possible to get themselves

on the pension, and I don't blame them, they were right, but I did some things inadvertently. The other thing you can't do is let somebody go who has been there, and I did that without being forewarned, so I was taken to court on that one. The guy I had to take his place I would then--if I had taken him back, I would then have to let him go and it got into all those things and I was up the creek no matter what, so I got them to let me go home. That's how I came back.
You were there for how long?
Twenty months or something like that. It was a three year contract.
Other than those hassles, how as living over there?
